profile.overview:
Wiscon Industries Limited is a Delhi-based supplier of consumer electronic products in India. Its product portfolio includes LED televisions, air coolers, washing machines, and air conditioners, which are sold under its flagship brand, Wiscon. The company also sells electric scooters under a third-party brand.
The company serves both business-to-business (B2B) and business-to-consumer (B2C) customers. It conducts its B2B operations through an offline customer network, while it makes B2C sales through its website. Wiscon Industries was incorporated as a public limited company on September 16, 2022. 
In May 2025, the company acquired a 100% stake in Dalmia Technologies Limited (DTL), which manufactures LED televisions and trades in other electronic products. DTL became its wholly owned subsidiary, and the company’s consolidated financial statements include DTL from FY26 onward. Accordingly, consolidated figures for FY26 and the quarter ended June 30, 2026 include DTL’s financial results, while historical figures for FY24 and FY25 in the relevant standalone statements reflect Wiscon Industries on a standalone basis.
Use of proceeds: 
The IPO consists of both a fresh issue of shares and an offer for sale (OFS).​ Proceeds from the OFS will go to the respective selling shareholders, whereas the net proceeds from the fresh issue will be utilised for the following purposes:​
Investment in the wholly owned subsidiary, Dalmia Technologies Limited for financing its capital expenditure towards purchase of plant and machinery — Rs 15.04 crore
Investment in Dalmia Technologies Limited for funding its incremental working capital requirements — Rs 35 crore
To meet working capital requirements of Wiscon— Rs 17 crore
To fund marketing and promotional activities in the company — Rs 5.22 crore
General corporate purposes

profile.overview:
Jio Platforms is a technology company that provides digital connectivity and digital services across India. Its subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm Limited, offers mobile connectivity, fixed broadband, and digital services. The company develops and operates its own technology stack, covering network infrastructure, device engineering, software, operating systems, and digital applications. Its technology portfolio includes 4G, 5G, cloud-native core network architectures, and AI-driven network automation. The company also develops digital products and technologies for consumers and businesses. 
As of June 30, 2026, Jio Platforms and its subsidiaries had applied for 7,220 patents in India and other countries across various digital technology areas. The company had 12,477 employees in its digital products and technology development team as of the same date. Its business combines digital connectivity infrastructure with software, applications, and other digital services.
Use of proceeds: 
This is a fresh issue of shares. Therefore, the net proceeds from the fresh issue will go to the company. They will be utilised for the following purposes:
Prepayment, in full or in part, of certain outstanding borrowings availed by the material subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm Limited (RJIL) — Rs 27,500 crore
General corporate purposes

strengths: Jio Platforms claims to have vertically integrated technology capabilities across network infrastructure, device engineering, software, operating systems, and digital applications. The company claims to operate an end-to-end 5G standalone technology stack nationwide, covering its core network, devices, and OSS/BSS operating systems. It also uses proprietary unlicensed band radio (UBR) technology to provide fixed wireless broadband connectivity, with bandwidth of up to 1 Gbps.

As of June 30, 2026, the company had access to a pan-India network comprising 360,537 network towers and over 1.0 million route kilometres of fibre. The company offers fixed broadband services through JioFiber and JioAirFiber. As of June 30, 2026, these services had a combined customer base of 28.6 million, while JioAirFiber had approximately 14.0 million customers.

Jio Platforms offers consumer applications such as MyJio, JioTV+, JioSaavn, JioAICloud, and JioGames, along with business solutions such as managed Wi-Fi and hybrid cloud services. As of June 30, 2026, JioTV+ aggregated over 1,000 digital TV channels and 15 OTT services.

The company uses its proprietary AI platform, JioBrain, for network capacity allocation, fault prediction, anomaly detection, and network optimisation. It also uses digital twin technology to assess network coverage, plan infrastructure rollouts, and guide field engineers during customer installations.
The company reported revenue from operations of Rs 146,885.3 crore and EBITDA of Rs 76,255.4 crore in FY26. Its net leverage ratio declined from 0.88 times in FY24 to 0.36 times in FY26.
risks: Jio Platforms has entered into various agreements with Reliance Industries Limited, Reliance Retail Limited, and other Reliance Group entities for project execution, business support, equipment supply, and distribution services. Reliance Retail Limited is the sole distributor of the company’s prepaid connectivity services, which contributed 76.37%, 77.88%, 77.08%, 78.57%, and 79.35% of consolidated revenue from operations in the three months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, and FY26, FY25, and FY24, respectively. Any disruption or termination of these arrangements could adversely affect the company’s business, financial condition, and results of operations.

Reliance Jio Infocomm Limited (RJIL), the company’s material subsidiary, contributed 87.74% of consolidated revenue from operations, 94.88% of EBITDA, and 93.76% of profit after tax in FY26. For the three months ended June 30, 2026, its contribution was 87.34%, 93.89%, and 92.31%, respectively. Any deterioration in RJIL’s business or financial performance due to competition, regulatory changes, technological disruption, or other adverse events could materially affect the company’s consolidated financial results. Further, the company’s key performance indicators primarily reflect RJIL’s digital connectivity services and may not adequately represent its technology platform business, potentially limiting investors’ ability to assess its performance in this area.

Jio Platforms depends on a limited number of service providers for passive network infrastructure. As of June 30, 2026, Summit Digitel Infrastructure Limited owned 174,451 of the 360,537 network towers used by the company, while Jio Digital Fibre Private Limited met approximately 98% of its optic fibre network requirements, excluding the last-mile fibre network owned by RJIL. RJIL has long-term agreements with both providers, which require minimum payments and do not permit termination by RJIL. Any disruption in tower or fibre availability, failure to meet service commitments, or relocation of infrastructure could cause network outages, service degradation, and customer losses, adversely affecting the company’s business and financial performance.

Jio Platforms’ systems, networks, applications, and data may be exposed to cybersecurity threats, including ransomware, phishing, malware, and data or privacy breaches. Although the company reported no successful cyberattacks or security breaches during the three months ended June 30, 2026, or FY24 to FY26, future incidents could require significant expenditure to investigate and resolve, disrupt operations, and damage its reputation. The company also relies on data centre infrastructure provided by its promoter in Jamnagar, Nagpur, and Mumbai, as well as third-party cloud hosting and edge infrastructure services. Any disruption or termination of these arrangements could affect service quality, increase customer churn, and adversely affect the company’s business and financial performance.

Jio Platforms’ telecommunications business is subject to extensive and evolving regulations covering licensing, spectrum usage, data privacy, and digital services. RJIL faces regulatory demands, including Rs 27.1 crore in financial disincentives imposed by TRAI for alleged violations relating to unsolicited commercial communications and service quality, which are under appeal. RJIL also faces a disputed additional spectrum usage charge demand of Rs 138.91 crore, which was set aside by TDSAT but is subject to an appeal before the Supreme Court. The company has previously incurred Rs 123.2 crore in non-performance penalties and liquidated damages for prolonged service interruptions in specified locations. Changes in licence fees, spectrum charges or other regulations, or failure to comply with applicable requirements, could increase costs, result in penalties or restrict services, adversely affecting the company’s business and financial performance.

Jio Platforms operates a capital-intensive business, with cash capital expenditure of Rs 34,184.3 crore in FY26, Rs 44,268 crore in FY25 and Rs 53,509.6 crore in FY24, representing 23.27%, 34.53% and 48.84% of revenue from operations, respectively. In FY26, network expenditure accounted for Rs 29,377.1 crore of cash capital expenditure. Significant spending on network expansion, technology upgrades, and digital platforms may take time to generate returns and depends on regulatory approvals, funding availability, and customer adoption. Cost overruns, delays, or lower-than-expected demand for new services could reduce the returns on these investments and adversely affect the company’s financial performance.

Fifteen subsidiaries of Jio Platforms incurred losses during the three months ended June 30, 2026, with combined losses after tax of Rs 20.5 crore. In FY26, 11 subsidiaries reported combined losses after tax of Rs 100.6 crore, compared with Rs 162.8 crore in FY25 and Rs 57.4 crore in FY24. Although these losses were not material to the company’s consolidated financial results during these periods, continued losses may require additional financial support or equity infusions by the company and could adversely affect its financial condition and results of operations.

profile.overview:
Sahajanand Medical Technologies Limited develops, manufactures, and sells medical devices used in vascular and structural heart interventions. Founded in 2001, the company offers vascular intervention products, including coronary stents and coronary balloon catheters, and structural heart products, including transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) devices and occluders. Its portfolio also includes renal stents, peripheral drug-coated balloons, and traded medical products.
The company markets its products through direct sales, hybrid, and distributor-led models. In FY26, it generated revenue from 77 countries, including India, with operations across Europe and other international markets. It currently operates three manufacturing facilities, two in India and one in Thailand. Additionally, it has two research and development centres, located in India and Thailand, focused on medical device development and product improvements.
Use of proceeds: 
The IPO is an offer-for-sale (OFS). The company will not receive any proceeds from the offer. Net proceeds from the offer will go to the promoter selling shareholders in proportion to the number of shares offered by them for sale.
The primary objective of the offer is to achieve the benefits of listing the equity shares on the stock exchanges, which is expected to enhance the company’s visibility and brand recognition. Listing will also provide liquidity to the existing shareholders and create a public market for the company’s shares in India​.

The company supplies its products to government defence agencies, law enforcement and homeland security agencies, and other defence equipment manufacturers in India and overseas.
The company operates an R&D centre in Bengaluru, Karnataka, where it undertakes product design, development and prototyping. profile.overview:

Any failure or disruption in procuring raw materials from these suppliers could affect manufacturing operations, product availability, and results of operations.

The company’s business is sensitive to seasonal variations and unpredictable weather conditions affecting agricultural activity. Erratic monsoons, droughts, and floods may disrupt farming cycles, reduce crop yields, and affect the timing and extent of agrochemical applications. Changes in pest patterns and extreme weather conditions may also affect demand for pesticides and fertilisers, potentially adversely impacting the company’s business, results of operations, and financial condition.

The company derives its entire revenue from the domestic Indian market, with significant dependence on Andhra Pradesh and Assam. Revenue from Andhra Pradesh stood at Rs 11.49 crore in FY26, Rs 15.21 crore in FY25 and Rs 4.58 crore in FY24, contributing 33.98%, 55.39% and 41.88%, respectively. Revenue from Assam was Rs 7.04 crore, Rs 6.37 crore and Rs 2.43 crore, contributing 20.82%, 23.19% and 22.23%, respectively. Any slowdown or adverse developments in these markets could adversely affect the company’s business, results of operations, and financial condition.
The company and its promoters are involved in ongoing criminal and material proceedings. Any adverse judgments in the cases could be detrimental to the company’s business prospects.

The company reported negative cash flows from operating activities of Rs 3.00 crore in FY25 and Rs 4.34 crore in FY24. Negative operating cash flows were primarily due to working capital deployment towards inventories and trade receivables. Investing cash flow was negative at Rs 2.91 crore in FY25 and Rs 1.32 crore in FY24, mainly due to purchases of property, plant and equipment and intangible assets of Rs 2.95 crore and Rs 1.32 crore, respectively. Financing cash flow was negative at Rs 2.32 crore in FY26, primarily due to interest and finance costs of Rs 1.34 crore, repayment of long-term borrowings of Rs 5.52 crore and repayment of short-term borrowings of Rs 1.05 crore. Continued negative cash flows could adversely affect the company’s liquidity, financial condition and ability to fund its operations and growth plans.
As of FY26, the company’s trade receivables were Rs 16.93 crore. Failure to collect these receivables on time, or at all, can negatively impact the business and its financial condition.
As of FY26, the company had outstanding financial indebtedness of Rs 7.27 crore. Any failure to service or repay these loans can harm the company’s operations and financial position.

blogs.title: IPO Basics: How Initial Public Offerings Work in India (SEBI T+3 Framework)
blogs.seoTitle: IPO Basics India – DRHP, Price Band, Lot Size & T+3 Listing Explained | PriceAlerter
blogs.metaDescription: Understand how Indian IPOs work from DRHP filing and anchor bidding to ASBA/UPI application, allotment, and T+3 listing on NSE and BSE.
blogs.author: PriceAlerter Editorial Research
blogs.excerpt: A complete guide to Mainboard and SME IPO structures, fresh issue vs Offer for Sale (OFS), book building, and the SEBI T+3 listing cycle.

toc.title: 1. What is an Initial Public Offering?
2. Fresh Issue vs. Offer for Sale (OFS)

sections.heading: 1. What is an Initial Public Offering?
paragraphs: An Initial Public Offering (IPO) is the process through which a privately held company raises equity capital from institutional and retail investors and lists its shares on stock exchanges such as the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE).

Before launching an IPO in India, the issuer files a Draft Red Herring Prospectus (DRHP) with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), disclosing audited historical financials, business risks, promoter shareholding, and objects of the issue.

sections.heading: 2. Fresh Issue vs. Offer for Sale (OFS)
paragraphs: Understanding the split between Fresh Issue and Offer for Sale is critical to evaluating capital deployment.
bullets: Fresh Issue: New shares are created and issued; proceeds flow directly into the company for capex, debt reduction, or working capital.
Offer for Sale (OFS): Existing promoters or private equity investors sell their stake; proceeds go to the selling shareholders rather than the company balance sheet.

sections.heading: 3. Mainboard vs. SME IPO Platforms
paragraphs: Mainboard IPOs typically carry smaller retail lot sizes (~₹14,000–₹15,000 per lot) and list on NSE/BSE main boards. SME IPOs list on NSE Emerge or BSE SME with minimum retail lot sizes exceeding ₹1,00,000 and higher post-listing liquidity risk.

sections.heading: 4. The SEBI T+3 Listing Timeline
paragraphs: Under SEBI’s mandatory T+3 framework, if an issue closes on Day T, allotment is finalized on T+1, refunds/unblocking and demat credit occur on T+2, and shares commence trading on T+3.

toc.title: 1. ASBA Bank Blocking vs. UPI Mandate
3. Why Cut-Off Price Matters for Retail

sections.heading: 1. ASBA Bank Blocking vs. UPI Mandate
paragraphs: All IPO applications in India use ASBA (Application Supported by Blocked Amount). Instead of debiting money upfront, your bank temporarily blocks the application amount in your savings account until allotment is finalized.
Retail applicants applying up to ₹5,00,000 can apply via broker apps using a UPI ID, provided they approve the UPI mandate request before 5:00 PM on the closing day.

sections.heading: 2. Retail, sNII, bNII & QIB Categories
paragraphs: SEBI classifies non-institutional and retail bidders strictly by application size:
bullets: Retail Individual Investor (RII): Up to ₹2,00,000 per PAN.
Big NII (bNII): Above ₹10,00,000 (must apply via bank ASBA netbanking).

sections.heading: 3. Why Cut-Off Price Matters for Retail
paragraphs: In oversubscribed book-built issues, the final issue price is almost always fixed at the upper end of the price band. Selecting the "Cut-Off Price" option ensures your bid remains valid at the final discovered price (available only to Retail and Employee categories).

blogs.title: IPO Allotment Explained: Proportional vs. Lottery Allocation & Registrar Check
blogs.seoTitle: IPO Allotment Process & How to Check Allotment Status | PriceAlerter
blogs.metaDescription: How registrars like KFinTech and Link Intime process oversubscribed IPO allotments, why single-lot applications work in Retail, and how to check status.
blogs.author: PriceAlerter Editorial Research
blogs.excerpt: Understand SEBI’s lottery allotment rule for oversubscribed Retail and sNII buckets, common rejection reasons, and official registrar verification.

sections.heading: 1. Oversubscribed Retail Lottery Rule
paragraphs: When the Retail category is subscribed more than 1x, SEBI rules mandate that every valid applicant should receive at least one minimum lot if possible. If applicants exceed available lots, the registrar runs a computerized random lottery.
Applying for multiple lots from the same PAN in an oversubscribed retail issue does not improve allotment odds compared to applying for 1 lot.

sections.heading: 2. Common Reasons Applications Get Rejected
paragraphs: Ensure technical accuracy before submitting bids:
bullets: Multiple applications submitted using the same PAN across different brokers.
UPI mandate left unapproved or expiring prior to issue closure.
Mismatch between bank account holder name/PAN and demat account PAN.

sections.heading: 3. Official Allotment Status Check
paragraphs: Always verify allotment directly on the official registrar portal (such as KFin Technologies, Link Intime, or Bigshare Services) or the NSE/BSE IPO verification pages using your PAN or Application Number.

blogs.title: IPO GMP Explained: What Grey Market Premium Means & Its Limitations
blogs.seoTitle: IPO GMP Explained – Formula, Risks & Unofficial Nature | PriceAlerter
blogs.metaDescription: Learn what IPO Grey Market Premium (GMP) is, how estimated listing price is calculated, and why unofficial GMP cannot predict guaranteed listing gains.
blogs.author: PriceAlerter Editorial Research
blogs.excerpt: A transparent breakdown of how unofficial grey market premiums form, how hypothetical listing estimates are calculated, and why fundamentals matter more.

toc.title: 3. Why GMP Is Not an Exchange Quote

sections.heading: 1. What is Grey Market Premium?
paragraphs: Grey Market Premium (GMP) refers to an unofficial, unregulated over-the-counter premium or discount at which IPO shares are quoted informally before official listing on NSE or BSE.
GMP is not recognized, regulated, or published by SEBI, NSE, or BSE.

sections.heading: 2. How Hypothetical Listing Estimates Work
paragraphs: Trackers compute a hypothetical reference price using the upper price band plus the latest unofficial GMP:
bullets: Estimated Listing Price = IPO Upper Issue Price + Latest GMP
Estimated Gain % = (Latest GMP / IPO Upper Issue Price) × 100

sections.heading: 3. Why GMP Is Not an Exchange Quote
paragraphs: Grey market quotes suffer from thin liquidity, speculative sentiment swings, and zero settlement guarantee. Broad market corrections between issue close and listing day frequently cause actual exchange opening prices to diverge sharply from prior GMP expectations.

blogs.title: Fundamental Analysis & Financial Ratios: P/E, P/B, ROE, ROCE & Debt-to-Equity
blogs.seoTitle: Financial Ratios for Indian Stocks – P/E, P/B, ROE, ROCE Explained | PriceAlerter
blogs.metaDescription: Master essential stock valuation and profitability ratios including P/E, P/B, ROE, ROCE, and Debt-to-Equity when analysing NSE/BSE companies and IPOs.
blogs.author: PriceAlerter Editorial Research
blogs.excerpt: How to read company financial statements, compare valuation multiples against industry peers, and avoid value traps using capital efficiency metrics.

sections.heading: 1. Valuation Multiples: P/E and P/B
paragraphs: Price-to-Earnings (P/E) compares a company’s share price to its Earnings Per Share (EPS). Always compare a stock or IPO’s P/E against listed sector peers using the same reporting period (TTM or FY26).
Price-to-Book (P/B) is especially vital for banks, NBFCs, and asset-heavy lenders where book value reflects tangible equity capital.

sections.heading: 2. Profitability: ROE vs. ROCE
paragraphs: Return on Equity (ROE = Net Profit / Shareholders’ Equity) measures return generated on equity capital, while Return on Capital Employed (ROCE = EBIT / Capital Employed) evaluates total operational efficiency across both debt and equity.

sections.heading: 3. Balance Sheet Safety: Debt-to-Equity
paragraphs: A rising ROE fueled by excessive borrowing is fragile during interest-rate upcycles. Checking Debt-to-Equity alongside interest coverage ensures earnings growth is backed by sustainable cash flow.

sections.heading: 1. NSE and BSE Market Structure
paragraphs: India’s equity trading centres on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), regulated by SEBI with T+1 equity settlement. Most large-cap and mid-cap stocks trade on both exchanges simultaneously.

sections.heading: 2. How NIFTY 50 and SENSEX Work
paragraphs: NIFTY 50 tracks 50 large, liquid Indian companies weighted by free-float market capitalization, while BSE SENSEX tracks 30 blue-chip leaders. Sectoral indices such as BANK NIFTY track concentrated banking performance.

sections.heading: 3. Direct Equities vs. Mutual Funds
paragraphs: Investors seeking diversified market exposure without single-stock research overhead often combine core index or flexi-cap mutual funds (regulated under AMFI/SEBI norms) with selective direct equity or IPO allocations.

sections.heading: 1. Valuation & Post-Listing Drawdown Risk
paragraphs: Not every IPO lists at a premium. Companies priced aggressively during peak market optimism can list below issue price or underperform if post-listing quarterly earnings miss prospectus projections.

sections.heading: 2. SME Board Liquidity & Circuit Limits
paragraphs: SME-listed equities trade in fixed lot sizes and often hit 5% or 20% circuit filters with thin order-book depth, making rapid exits difficult during risk-off sessions.

sections.heading: 3. Position Sizing & Verified Research
paragraphs: Always cross-verify financial statements in the official RHP/Prospectus, separate speculative GMP chatter from balance-sheet quality, and size individual equity bets conservatively within your overall asset allocation.

blogs.author: PriceAlerter Editorial Research
blogs.excerpt: Skip the 400-page overwhelm: focus on Objects of the Issue, working capital intensity, contingent liabilities, related-party transactions, and peer valuation.

toc.title: 1. Objects of the Issue & Fresh vs. OFS Split
3. Restated Cash Flows vs. Accounting Profit

sections.heading: 1. Objects of the Issue & Fresh vs. OFS Split
paragraphs: Every Red Herring Prospectus (RHP) opens with a concise summary of capital deployment. Distinguish carefully between Fresh Issue proceeds funding productive capacity or debt repayment versus Offer for Sale (OFS) exits by early financial sponsors or promoters.
Watch out for vague "General Corporate Purposes" exceeding 25% of issue proceeds or sudden pre-IPO debt spikes slated for repayment using public funds.
bullets: Check exact capex milestones and scheduled commercial operation dates.
Verify promoter lock-in periods (typically 18 months for minimum promoter contribution and 6 months for remaining pre-IPO equity).

sections.heading: 2. Material Risk Factors & Pending Litigations
paragraphs: Do not treat the Internal Risk Factors section as boilerplate. Pay close attention to customer concentration (whether Top 5 clients contribute over 50% of revenue), single-geography factory exposure, regulatory license renewals, and tax or criminal proceedings involving directors or group entities.

sections.heading: 3. Restated Cash Flows vs. Accounting Profit
paragraphs: Compare three-year Restated Consolidated PAT against Operating Cash Flow (OCF) and Trade Receivables days. A company reporting rapid profit expansion while operating cash flow remains persistently negative may face working capital stress or aggressive revenue recognition.

sections.heading: 4. Related-Party Transactions & Promoter Track Record
paragraphs: Inspect Related-Party Transactions (RPT) in the financial notes for raw-material purchases, factory lease rentals, or brand royalties paid to promoter-owned private entities. Transparent governance lowers post-listing minority shareholder risk.

blogs.seoTitle: STCG & LTCG Tax Rules on Indian IPOs & Stocks | PriceAlerter
blogs.metaDescription: Understand how Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG), Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG), STT, holding periods, and dividend income are taxed on NSE and BSE equities in India.
blogs.author: PriceAlerter Editorial Research
blogs.excerpt: An investor reference on holding period classification (12-month threshold), listing-day sell tax implications, STT applicability, and AIS/Form 26AS reconciliation.

toc.title: 1. Holding Period: Demat Credit Date to Sell Date

sections.heading: 1. Holding Period: Demat Credit Date to Sell Date
paragraphs: For IPO shares allotted in India, the holding period for Income Tax purposes commences from the date shares are allotted/credited to your demat account, not the application bid date.
Listed equity shares sold on recognized Indian exchanges (NSE/BSE) where Securities Transaction Tax (STT) is paid qualify as Long-Term Capital Assets only if held for more than 12 months.

sections.heading: 2. Short-Term vs. Long-Term Equity Gains
paragraphs: Selling IPO shares on listing day or within 12 months triggers Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG) under Section 111A of the Income Tax Act (20% base rate plus applicable surcharge and 4% cess under post-July 2024 Finance Act rules).

Equity holdings sold after 12 months qualify for Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) under Section 112A (12.5% rate above the ₹1.25 lakh annual aggregate exemption threshold, without indexation). Always consult a qualified Chartered Accountant for your personal slab and surcharge rules.

sections.heading: 3. Dividends, STT & Tax Record-Keeping
paragraphs: Equity dividends received from NSE/BSE companies are taxable at your marginal income tax slab rate, with 10% TDS deducted when annual dividends from a company exceed statutory limits. Reconcile your broker Profit & Loss statement with the Income Tax AIS portal before filing ITR-2 or ITR-3.
